instructions:
Graduation: write your own cheat sheet, in Neovim of course.

Create ~/vimdrill/cheatsheet.md with at least 40 non-empty lines: the commands
YOU actually use, grouped your way (motions, operators, text objects, search, registers,
macros, ex commands, windows, your mappings, LSP keys...). Write each entry in your own words.
Save the first time with :w ++p, which also creates the ~/vimdrill folder.

Ideas while writing it:
- :r !vimdrill --show 4.2   reads a lesson card into the buffer to start from
- use macros and :s to format your list, gq to wrap long lines, gcc to comment out drafts
- go through the lessons you found hardest (/vim-daily knows your misses) and write those down

Then run: vimdrill --check
